name: Cloud Media Shrinker
subtitle: Compress photos and videos
privacyPolicyURLStatus: Source prepared locally; publish and verify this URL before submission
description:
Find the photos and videos taking up space, preview them, and choose what to keep.

Cloud Media Shrinker works with Apple Photos, local folders and folders from Google Drive for desktop. Compression runs on your Mac. Your media is not uploaded to the developer.

Choose video resolution, frame rate, format and quality. Keep the original resolution when you want smaller files without resizing. HDR video stays HDR. Compression is lossy, and results vary by the original footage and settings.

Make smaller HEIC copies of supported RAW and JPEG photos, or keep only the still image of a Live Photo. Review the result before deleting an original.

The app keeps a local savings history so you can see what changed. Original deletion is always your choice. Apple Photos deletions go to Recently Deleted; folder deletions use the appropriate trash.

Google Drive support requires Google Drive for desktop. Space in cloud storage may not be reclaimed until originals leave Recently Deleted or the service's trash.

Compatibility and the behavior of Photos items with unavailable sizes must be finalized before this description is submitted.
reviewNotesDraft:
No Cloud Media Shrinker account or subscription is required. The app processes media locally. It uses PhotoKit to access a Photos library after permission, and user-selected folder access for local and Google Drive folders. Google Drive is an optional source through Google's desktop app; the Apple Photos and Local Folder sources work independently.

The bundled interface uses WKWebView and a server bound only to 127.0.0.1. Incoming and outgoing network entitlements support that local interface and system media access. It does not expose the server on the local network. App Store builds have no GitHub update checker.

The Photos scripting-targets entitlement allows copying titles, captions and keywords to compressed copies, and showing selected items in Photos. If metadata cannot be copied, the app keeps the original.

Test with disposable media: add a folder, pick Compress on a video, keep original resolution, start the queue, then play the smaller copy in the Compressed subfolder. Leave original deletion off. Photos permission and metadata preservation still require validation on the sandboxed candidate before submission.

For size measurement on older macOS, the user selects their System Photo Library through NSOpenPanel. The app stores a read-only security-scoped bookmark, opens Photos.sqlite with SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY, and reads size metadata. It also reads the logical sizes of local adjustment metadata files, without opening media. It never writes to the Photos database. PhotoKit is used for library access and media operations. Unsupported or stale size records are shown as unavailable rather than downloading originals.
